text: Adopted the Kolmogorov axioms as the measure-theoretic foundation for the seminar notes; non-negativity, unit total mass, and countable additivity on a sigma-algebra anchor every later proof.

queries.text: which axiom system grounds the seminar notes and which three clauses does it rest on
kolmogorov axiom sigma algebra countable additivity measure foundation

text: Andrey Kolmogorov published Grundbegriffe der Wahrscheinlichkeitsrechnung in 1933, framing probability as a normalised measure on a sigma-algebra and displacing the Laplace-era combinatorial view.

queries.text: which 1933 monograph recast probability as a measure and whose combinatorial framing did it displace
kolmogorov grundbegriffe 1933 measure sigma algebra laplace combinatorial

text: Durrett's Probability: Theory and Examples is the reference textbook for the measure-theoretic track; the fifth edition's martingale chapter drives the proofs in week nine.

queries.text: which textbook anchors the measure-theoretic track and which chapter feeds the martingale proofs
durrett probability theory examples martingale measure textbook reference

text: A sigma-algebra is the closure of a collection of subsets under complement and countable union; the Borel sigma-algebra on the real line is generated by the open intervals.

queries.text: which closure properties define a sigma-algebra and which generating family yields the Borel one
sigma algebra complement countable union borel real open interval

text: The Caratheodory extension theorem promotes a premeasure on an algebra to a unique countably additive measure on the generated sigma-algebra; Lebesgue measure is the canonical example.

queries.text: which theorem lifts a premeasure on an algebra to a measure on its generated sigma-algebra
caratheodory extension premeasure lebesgue measure sigma algebra algebra

text: A random variable is defined as a measurable function from a probability space into the real line; the pushforward measure gives the distribution without tying it to any sample space.

queries.text: how does the measure-theoretic framing define a random variable and derive its distribution
random variable measurable function pushforward distribution probability space

text: The Bernoulli distribution models a single coin flip with success probability p; summing n independent Bernoulli draws gives a binomial, which the lecture introduces as the first non-trivial pmf.

queries.text: which single-trial distribution sums into the binomial and how is it parametrised in the lecture
bernoulli binomial pmf coin flip success probability sum independent

text: The Poisson distribution arises as the n-to-infinity limit of a binomial with np held fixed; rare-event counts on a fixed interval are the canonical application in the queueing notes.

queries.text: which limiting argument derives the Poisson from the binomial and where does it get applied
poisson binomial limit np rare event queueing interval count

text: The geometric distribution counts the number of Bernoulli trials up to the first success; the negative binomial generalises to r successes and inherits memorylessness only in the geometric case.

queries.text: which discrete distribution counts trials to first success and how does the negative binomial extend it
geometric negative binomial bernoulli memoryless success trial count

text: The departmental espresso machine lost its steam wand over the weekend and two postdocs left a sticky note demanding biscotti restitution.
The normal distribution shows up as the Gaussian limit in the central limit theorem; the log-normal applies after exponentiating, and multiplicative-noise models in finance prefer it.

queries.text: which limit theorem yields the normal and which transformation produces the log-normal used in finance
normal log normal central limit theorem gaussian finance exponential

text: Exponential and gamma distributions model waiting times: exponential for a single Poisson event, gamma for the sum of k exponentials, with the shape parameter controlling tail behaviour.

queries.text: how do exponential and gamma distributions relate and which parameter controls their tails
exponential gamma waiting time poisson event shape tail parameter

text: Beta is the conjugate prior for Bernoulli and binomial likelihoods; the Dirichlet extends the story to the multinomial, which the topic-model notes lean on heavily.

queries.text: which conjugate pairings power the topic-model notes from binary up to categorical
beta dirichlet multinomial bernoulli conjugate prior topic model

text: Cauchy distribution's undefined mean and infinite variance make it a preferred counterexample for teaching why moment existence cannot be assumed in limit theorems.

queries.text: which distribution serves as the go-to counterexample for failed moment hypotheses in limit theorems
cauchy undefined mean infinite variance counterexample limit moment

text: Chi-squared distribution is the sum of k independent squared standard normals; the Student's t is the ratio of a standard normal to a scaled chi-squared, linking them in the testing chapter.

queries.text: how do chi-squared and Student's t connect through the standard normal in the testing chapter
chi squared student t standard normal ratio sum squared testing

text: Weibull and Pareto distributions model heavy-tailed lifetimes; the Weibull's shape parameter tunes bathtub-curve regions and the Pareto captures the eighty-twenty wealth asymptote.

queries.text: which two heavy-tailed distributions model lifetimes and wealth and what tunes their shapes
weibull pareto heavy tail lifetime shape bathtub wealth asymptote

text: Expectation of a random variable is the Lebesgue integral against the underlying probability measure; when a density exists the textbook collapses it to the familiar integral on the real line.

queries.text: how does the measure-theoretic definition of expectation reduce to the density-based integral
expectation lebesgue integral density probability measure random variable

text: Variance is defined as the expected squared deviation from the mean; covariance extends to two variables and correlation normalises it to the [-1, 1] interval regardless of scale.

queries.text: how do variance, covariance, and correlation nest and which one is scale-free
variance covariance correlation mean deviation scale free normalise

text: The moment generating function encodes all moments when it exists in a neighbourhood of zero; the characteristic function replaces it when moments fail, because it exists for every distribution.

queries.text: why does the characteristic function take over when the moment generating function fails to exist
moment generating characteristic function exist neighborhood moments zero

text: Jensen's inequality says the expectation of a convex function dominates the convex function of the expectation; the notes use it to derive the entropy lower bound in the variational inference section.

queries.text: how does Jensen's inequality underwrite the entropy lower bound in the variational inference notes
jensen inequality convex expectation variational inference entropy bound

text: Markov and Chebyshev inequalities bound tail probabilities by moments; Markov on a non-negative variable and Chebyshev through the variance are the two starter tools of concentration theory.

queries.text: which two elementary tail inequalities open the concentration-theory chapter and what do they use
markov chebyshev inequality tail moment variance concentration bound

text: Cauchy-Schwarz on expectations bounds the covariance by the product of standard deviations; the derivation goes through the discriminant of a quadratic in a real parameter t.

queries.text: which classical inequality bounds covariance by the product of standard deviations via a quadratic trick
cauchy schwarz covariance standard deviation quadratic discriminant bound

text: The Law of large numbers comes in weak and strong forms; the weak version needs only pairwise uncorrelated and bounded variance, while the strong version requires almost-sure convergence arguments.

queries.text: what separates the weak from the strong law of large numbers in the convergence requirements
law large numbers weak strong almost sure convergence uncorrelated

text: The central limit theorem says that a standardised sum of iid finite-variance variables converges in distribution to a standard normal; Lindeberg's condition relaxes the identically-distributed assumption.

queries.text: which extension of the central limit theorem drops the identically distributed assumption
central limit theorem lindeberg condition iid finite variance normal

text: Martingales are defined relative to a filtration: a process whose conditional expectation at the next step equals the current value; the gambler's fair-wealth model is the canonical example.

queries.text: how does a martingale relate to a filtration and which gambling model serves as the canonical example
martingale filtration conditional expectation gambler fair wealth

text: Doob's optional stopping theorem says bounded stopping times preserve the martingale property; the ABRACADABRA expected-hitting-time calculation is the standard application in the textbook.

queries.text: which theorem preserves martingale properties under bounded stopping and where is it applied
doob optional stopping martingale abracadabra hitting time bounded

text: Doob's maximal inequality bounds the probability that a non-negative submartingale exceeds a level by the terminal expectation over that level; it anchors the path-regularity proofs in chapter ten.

queries.text: which Doob inequality anchors the path-regularity proofs and what quantity does it bound
doob maximal inequality submartingale path regularity level terminal

text: Brownian motion is the almost-surely continuous martingale with independent Gaussian increments of variance equal to the time increment; the Levy characterisation pins it down uniquely.

queries.text: which characterisation pins down Brownian motion uniquely among continuous martingales
brownian motion martingale gaussian increment levy characterisation continuous

text: Markov chains transition according to a time-homogeneous kernel depending only on the current state; the memoryless property is what collapses the joint distribution into a product of transitions.

queries.text: how does the memoryless property collapse a Markov-chain joint distribution into transition products
markov chain transition kernel time homogeneous memoryless joint

text: An irreducible aperiodic Markov chain admits a unique stationary distribution that coincides with the long-run empirical frequency; reversibility lets detailed balance certify the stationary vector.

queries.text: which structural conditions guarantee a unique stationary distribution and which shortcut certifies it
irreducible aperiodic markov stationary detailed balance reversible unique

text: Mixing time is the first step at which the total-variation distance to the stationary distribution drops below a quarter; spectral gap bounds give the standard upper estimate.

queries.text: how is mixing time formally defined and which spectral quantity gives the standard upper bound
mixing time total variation stationary spectral gap quarter bound

text: Monte Carlo methods estimate expectations by averaging over iid samples from the target; variance of the estimator scales as one over root-n regardless of dimension, which is the selling point.

queries.text: which sampling strategy gives a one-over-root-n estimator variance independent of dimension
monte carlo iid sample expectation variance root n dimension

text: Metropolis-Hastings proposes a move from a kernel and accepts with the ratio that enforces detailed balance with respect to the target; symmetric proposals collapse the acceptance to the density ratio.

queries.text: which acceptance rule enforces detailed balance in Metropolis-Hastings and how does symmetry simplify it
metropolis hastings proposal acceptance detailed balance symmetric density

text: Gibbs sampling updates each coordinate from its full conditional given the rest; the cost per sweep is cheap in conjugate models, which is why hierarchical Bayes uses it as the first default.

queries.text: which MCMC sampler is the first default in hierarchical Bayes and why is it cheap there
gibbs sampling full conditional hierarchical bayes conjugate default

text: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo augments the target with a momentum variable and runs a symplectic leapfrog for proposals; the long-range moves beat random-walk Metropolis on correlated continuous posteriors.

queries.text: which MCMC variant uses symplectic leapfrog dynamics and what failure of random-walk Metropolis drives it
hamiltonian monte carlo momentum leapfrog random walk metropolis

text: Variational inference turns posterior inference into optimisation: fit a tractable family by maximising the ELBO, which is Jensen's lower bound on the log marginal likelihood.

queries.text: which objective converts posterior inference into optimisation and which inequality justifies it
variational inference elbo jensen marginal likelihood optimisation tractable

text: Preferred the measure-theoretic construction of conditional expectation over the elementary one; the Radon-Nikodym derivative handles null-event conditioning without the zero-divided-by-zero embarrassment.

queries.text: why does the measure-theoretic conditional expectation handle null-event conditioning gracefully
measure theoretic conditional expectation radon nikodym null event

text: Feller's An Introduction to Probability Theory and Its Applications, Volume II, is the recommended reference for the semimartingale and renewal-theory detours in the second half of the course.

entities.name: An Introduction to Probability Theory and Its Applications

relationships.source: An Introduction to Probability Theory and Its Applications
An Introduction to Probability Theory and Its Applications

queries.text: which classical two-volume work supports the renewal-theory and semimartingale material later in the course
feller introduction probability applications volume semimartingale renewal

text: Grenander and Szego's Toeplitz Forms and Their Applications supplies the spectral-density arguments used to analyse stationary Gaussian processes in the time-series week.

queries.text: which classical monograph supplies spectral-density arguments for stationary Gaussian processes
grenander szego toeplitz forms stationary gaussian spectral density

text: The convergence framework ranks almost-sure, in-probability, in-distribution, and in-Lp; the arrows only reverse under extra conditions like uniform integrability, which is the week-six gotcha.

queries.text: which hierarchy ranks the four convergence modes and which condition lets stronger modes follow weaker ones
convergence almost sure probability distribution lp uniform integrability

text: The filtration-adapted stochastic integral construction stalled without a clean extension past simple processes; the Ito isometry fixed the gap by giving an L2 density route for the general case.

queries.text: which isometry rescued the stochastic integral construction past simple processes via an L2 route
ito isometry stochastic integral filtration adapted simple process l2

text: The variational inference pipeline stalled on a discrete-latent categorical posterior where the reparameterisation trick does not apply; switched to a Gumbel-softmax relaxation to restore gradient flow.

queries.text: which relaxation fixed the discrete-latent gradient problem in the variational inference pipeline
variational inference gumbel softmax reparameterisation categorical discrete

text: The hallway printer insists on a 90-second warm-up every morning and the department intern swears it times its sulking with the kettle.
Detected non-converging chains in the MCMC diagnostics through split R-hat staying above 1.1 for more than five thousand iterations; reparametrised the hierarchical variance to a non-centered form.

queries.text: which diagnostic flagged the hierarchical chain problem and which reparametrisation restored mixing
mcmc diagnostics split r hat non centered hierarchical variance

text: Preferred the ergodic-theorem framing over the stationary-distribution framing when introducing MCMC convergence; time averages along a path are what practitioners actually compute in code.

queries.text: which framing wins for teaching MCMC convergence because it matches what code actually computes
ergodic theorem stationary distribution mcmc time average path code

text: Settled a long debate by picking Metropolis-adjusted Langevin over plain HMC for the sparse Bayesian regression because a single gradient step per iteration kept the inner loop cheap enough to mini-batch.

queries.text: which gradient MCMC won the bake-off against HMC for sparse Bayesian regression and why
metropolis adjusted langevin hmc sparse bayesian gradient mini batch

text: Shipped the martingale week of the course notes with Doob's decomposition, the optional stopping theorem, and the backwards martingale convergence theorem as the three load-bearing milestones.

queries.text: which three martingale results carry the week of course notes that just shipped
martingale doob decomposition optional stopping backwards convergence week

text: Reached the milestone of typing up the central limit theorem via characteristic functions with Levy's continuity theorem as the closing step; the classical moment proof stays only as an appendix exercise.

queries.text: which continuity theorem closed the characteristic-function proof of the central limit theorem in the notes
central limit theorem characteristic function levy continuity proof

text: Added a chapter milestone for the Poisson process as a counting martingale, including the compensator construction and the Watanabe characterisation linking it back to martingale theory.

queries.text: which Poisson-process milestone landed and which characterisation ties it to martingale theory
poisson process counting martingale compensator watanabe characterisation

text: Chose Markov-chain Monte Carlo over importance sampling for the high-dimensional posterior after the effective sample size of importance weights collapsed under dimension scaling past ten parameters.

queries.text: which sampler replaced importance sampling for the high-dimensional posterior and what signal drove it
mcmc importance sampling effective sample size dimension high dimensional
